{"basis":"measured","confidence":1.0,"fact_type":"finding","statement":"**ONE ROCKSDB STORE SERVES EVERY GIT BRANCH, SO THE LIVE GRAPH DOES NOT BRANCH — AND THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS A WORKFLOW RULE NOTHING STATES: YOU CANNOT HAVE TWO OPEN PULL REQUESTS THAT BOTH MAKE GRAPH WRITES.**

OBSERVED 2026-08-14 while holding PR #182 open (design-record writes) and being asked to build the command coverage accepted in it. `.reflow2/graph` is a single store shared by whatever branch is checked out; `git checkout <branch>` does not switch it. So any export taken on a second branch carries **the first branch's uncommitted graph writes too**, and both PRs then contain each other's nodes.

⇒ **THE CALL MADE, AND WHY:** the command-coverage build was FOLDED INTO #182 rather than opened as a third PR. **One PR at a time while graph writes are outstanding.** The alternative — branching from main and exporting — would have produced an export containing #182's nodes with a `prev_content_hash` pointing at main, i.e. a document silently claiming work that another open PR also claims. `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` and `dec:export-once-per-pr` constrain the export WITHIN a branch and say nothing about two branches sharing one store.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED HERE:** the collision was avoided rather than reproduced. What is established is the mechanism (one store, no per-branch isolation) and the decision taken because of it — not an observed corrupted export. A deliberate reproduction would be cheap and has not been done.

═══ ⭐ THE SERVED-SURFACE GAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT REACHES ANYONE ELSE ═══

**THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND IS SERVED — `parallel-work` sets up an isolated worktree with its own copy of the graph, which is exactly the isolation missing above. But the skill is framed by PEOPLE, not by BRANCHES:** *"Use when two or more people (or agents) need to work on one design at the same time without colliding — 'my brother and I are both editing this'."*

🛑 **ONE PERSON WITH TWO BRANCHES HITS THE IDENTICAL COLLISION AND WILL NOT REACH FOR A SKILL ABOUT COLLABORATING.** Every trigger phrase it lists is social; none is *"I have two PRs open"*. So the person most likely to hit this — a solo maintainer working two changes — is the one the skill's own trigger conditions exclude. That is AGENTS.md rule 7's shape: the lesson is real, and the served surface that would carry it does not currently invite the case.

📌 RELATED BUT DISTINCT, so this is not filed as a duplicate of any of them: `dec:multi-writer-architecture` covers the FILE as transport between people; `ver:merge-driver` covers merging the exported document; `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` and `fact:the-lineage-gate-verdict-depends-on-when-you-run-it` cover the chain WITHIN one branch. **None addresses two branches sharing one live store**, which is the only reason the fold-into-one-PR decision was needed.

⇒ OPEN, AND NOT PROPOSED AS A CHANGE HERE: whether `parallel-work`'s trigger conditions should name the solo-with-two-branches case, or whether something should notice that the store has writes belonging to a branch you are not on. Both are the owner's call.

═══ RECURRED 2026-09-06, FOUR TIMES IN ONE SESSION — appended, nothing above changed ═══

The 'avoided rather than reproduced' caveat above is now closed: the collision was REPRODUCED, as the gate refusing. (1) #431 and #430 both chained from the same main export; whichever merged second needed a re-export (done by merge order: 430 first, then 431 rebased and re-exported). (2) The enum PR's branch, cut while #434 was open, FAILED reflow2_check with five DRIFT findings — exactly #434's artifacts — because the shared store already held #434's checksum accepts and new test artifact while the branch's tree had main's files. The export from the shared store faithfully carried the sibling's claims and the tree could not satisfy them. (3) On that same branch `git pull --rebase` on main was refused for uncommitted work carried across the checkout — the one-store-per-directory shape again, seen from git's side. (4) Convention (i) was deliberately NOT started until #435 merged, for the same reason.

THE REMEDY THAT WORKED, stated as the rule the top of this fact says nothing states: **while a sibling PR with graph writes is open, do not export on a new branch; land the sibling, then re-point the new branch at the new main (`git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` carrying the working changes), restore main's export, re-export, and gate.** THE REMEDY REJECTED, with the reason: stacking the new PR on the sibling's branch — #427 was auto-CLOSED by GitHub when its base branch was deleted at merge (2026-09-05), so stacking trades a gate failure for a lost PR. Cherry-picking the sibling into the new branch was also rejected: it makes the new PR a superset and its squash-merge rebase conflict-prone.

WHAT THIS RECURRENCE SAYS ABOUT THE OPEN QUESTION ABOVE: four collisions in one day by one person on one machine is the solo-with-two-branches case exactly; the isolation `parallel-work` serves would have prevented all four, and nothing pointed at it. The cost was roughly forty minutes of re-exporting across the day, none of it lost work.

═══ RECURRED 2026-09-14/15, THREE MORE TIMES IN ONE SESSION — appended, nothing above changed ═══

(5) #509 and #510, both open from the one store: each export carried the other's checksums and neither could pass the coherence gate; folded into #510 by cherry-picking the code commits onto main and exporting once. (6) The v0.61.0 release branch, cut while #511 (an OpenCode plugin written by another session) was open: six DRIFT findings, all #511's artifacts — two `missing_artifact`, four `checksum_change` — from a store that held #511's registrations while the release tree had main's files; resolved by merging #511 first, rebasing the release onto it keeping only the version commit, restoring main's export and exporting once. (7) The three-leg import fix, built while #515 (a lockfile refresh) was open: not exported at all until #515 merged, then rebased and exported — the serialise-before-export remedy applied in advance, at the cost of the fix waiting on an unrelated CI run. Same mechanism every time; the serialise remedy above held all three times and is now the working rule of this repository even though nothing served states it. A fourth collision was pre-empted by the same means (the deps branch was reset onto main after #514 rather than exported alongside it).
